669	## Edge Cases
670	
671	*Format.* Each case is `If [condition]: [exact outcome]. [rationale]`, ends in its owner's rule-id (Boarding adds no behaviour, BS-1, so an outcome is always an owner's), and carries its id `EC-BS-n` at the end of the bold condition. Cases are grouped by theme; the audit additions of the checkpoint (K15: a DESTROYED node, a store module, a restore in `IN_POD`, the stowed plate, the door that mixes cold) are EC-BS-3, EC-BS-4, EC-BS-40, EC-BS-45 and EC-BS-20, and the dead-bus case (K4) is EC-BS-17. Numbers are design-time and rest on D.1 to D.10. Web Map's constants are registered [PLACEHOLDER] values (see the Format note of Core Rules).
672	
673	### A. Zero, maximum and out of range
674	
675	- **If the player presses `begin_cut` with the welder in hand (`START_EQUIPPED_SLOT` 2) or with no cutter in hand (EC-BS-1)**: the verb answers `NO_TOOL` as an outcome after the press, nothing is cut and no tool-channel tick accrues; `equip_tool` to slot 1 is the fix and its duration is unregistered, so every sortie time stays a lower bound (BS-2 step 1; IA-5, SE-11, SN OQ-SN-6). The wrong tool is an honest, cheap failure, not a hidden gate.
676	- **If the player presses `begin_cap` while carrying, or tries to `equip_tool` the welder with hands full (EC-BS-2)**: both are `BUSY`; the cap is a bare-handed welder act, so the order is cut, cap, then pick up, which follows from "never auto-carried" and not from a rule (BS-8, BS-9; IA-28, SE-11). A second `begin_cap` on an already capped stub is `INVALID_TARGET` (IA-26).
677	- **If the node being cut is DESTROYED (EC-BS-3)**: the cut yields `scrap_count` of its repair part and **no module**; there is nothing to carry, the parts are STOWED stock (they ride the body, not the hands), and the cut's noise is spent regardless. A DESTROYED machine is the loudest thing in its room and was never worth a module (IDB-17, LSG:772; K15).
678	- **If the module being cut is a store (the bus battery `b_a2`, the lamp battery `b_a1`) (EC-BS-4)**: its `stock` is discarded into the Graph's `discarded_*` counters so the conservation invariant still closes, and a reinstalled store starts at stock 0 (IDB-18 (i)). A battery has no fluid port, so it leaves no stub; the island re-solves on the next run and what ran on it goes dark, `b_a1` being the stored energy behind A's one residual lamp (DA-27, `[derived]`), so cutting it ends the visible unknown and is a cost the player caused (IDB-18, K15).
679	- **If a second module is wanted while one is carried (EC-BS-5)**: `pickup` answers `BUSY`; the player drops the first in a safe room and shuttles, or leaves it for a second hop, and a second hop costs a second `HOP_FUEL_ML` [PLACEHOLDER] (D.6). The spare `mod_breaker_junction` and `htr_a` cannot ride in the same hop (IA-28, SE-12).
680	- **If a stowed stack cannot take the pickup (a glowstick shelf of 2 with 3 already stowed, or a second `part_hull_plate`) (EC-BS-6)**: the pickup is rejected with Suit's immediate `STACK_FULL`, nothing is taken and nothing is deleted; the stack stays on the shelf and the player throws or uses one first. `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX` [PLACEHOLDER] 4 and the plate's `stack_max` 1 are the structural bound (IA-28, SE-12, IDB-15).
681	- **If the player holds a tool in the HAND holder when a CARRIED-class yield is picked up (EC-BS-7)**: the pickup is admitted, because "needs hands free" means no carried instance and a held tool is a different holder (SE-12). Recorded as an ask to Interaction to confirm the wording (ASK-BS-I5); until then the sortie tests treat it as admitted (IA-28).
682	
683	### B. The carry-admitted set, doors and drops
684	
685	- **If the console row is refused and the player presses the pod console while carrying (EC-BS-8)**: the press is `BUSY` with no prompt; the module must be dropped first and stays aboard exactly as left, persisting on the dormant derelict, and the carry-home branch is lost. **This state is not shippable for the MVP (BS-9):** it removes the carry home, the loop the MVP exists to test, so the producer treats the refusal as a stop and not a degrade. With a BREACH running it would be the abandon cost, but the failure escalates to the producer as a design blocker and is not an accepted state (BS-9 fallback; C-BS-1; IA-5, WM-24).
686	- **If the carried def is not in the focused hardpoint's `compatible_defs` (EC-BS-9)**: there is no prompt at all, an immediate answer that reads only the carried def and the hardpoint's declaration and never a module-body field, so it is not an oracle (BS-18; MSA-26, IA-11).
687	- **If a FAILED-`hp` instance is installed (EC-BS-10)**: it installs as a FAILED module, `condition_bp` carrying through unchanged, and the home island treats it as dead; no verb refused the install and no reason named the condition, and the consequence is visible in the Graph's channel (a dark lantern, a dry trail, no output) (BS-18; IDB-17, IDB-18, LS-22).
688	- **If a CLOSED door lies on the carry route (the home `door_cargo_s`, or a door the player shut behind them) (EC-BS-11)**: the door face shows its ordinary V4 plate and `set_opening` is Applied (not `BUSY`); the carrier presses it, waits `DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS` 30 [PLACEHOLDER] and walks through with `carry_ref` unchanged; a door shut as a containment tool is the player's own cost on the way out; during a TELL or BREACH the legal alternative is to abandon the module (BS-10, BS-13; IA-5, IA-24, IA-28). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
689	- **If every candidate cell for a `drop` is blocked (a threshold square, nine blocked cells) (EC-BS-12)**: `drop` answers immediate `OBSTRUCTED` and the module stays carried; the player steps back a tile and tries again. Door cells answer `NONE` from `floor_tile_at`, so a drop never lands on one, and A and B corridors are 3 wide, so the risk cells are door thresholds only (BS-10; IA-28, DA-7).
690	- **If a SYSTEM-origin close targets a door whose leaf overlaps a carrier's foot box (EC-BS-13)**: the attempt becomes `CLOSING_BLOCKED` and retries every tick, landing on the first clear tick; the carrier reopens it with the ordinary press (BS-10) at `DOOR_ATTEMPT_TICKS` they did not choose. MVP content has no SYSTEM close on a carry route, and a content change that adds one costs a carrier that surprise, which is why it stays an ask (BS-10; IA-24, ASK-BS-I2). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
691	- **If a module is dropped and its section is then welded or cut away before the pickup (EC-BS-14)**: the loose item's position is `(section_id, pos_px)` section-local, so it goes with its section; a section that is cut away takes it with the Graph's `discarded_*` bookkeeping, a loss that belongs to the cut's owner (BS-23; LY-22, LS-16).
692	
693	### C. The cut, the stubs and the faucet
694	
695	- **If the machine being cut is running (the home scrubber, `htr_a` on a woken bus) (EC-BS-15)**: the cut is legal with no special case; the island re-solves on the next run, its dependants go STARVE, and the hum of the thing being cut drops: true-state audio in the consequence channel (LSG:976) that is not in LSG:44's enumerated list, used as true-state corroboration and not the falsifier of record until the Graph rules. The player who cuts their own air has made a P1 choice the world shows at once (BS-7, BS-4; LSG:773, FT:207, C-BS-4).
696	- **If `scr_a` is cut and carried home (EC-BS-16)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: it is a legal cut whose carry ends at a vacant scrubber hardpoint (the committed content route, user ruling D72), where `install_module` is offered by the same plate whether the instance is FAILED or healthy (no oracle, IA-11) and installs it as what it is: a FAILED `scr_a` installs a FAILED module with no take-back (no `remove_module`, MSA-28), in a hardpoint that a healthy module could have filled. That is the stake of the read, and the reference cut stays `htr_a` (BS-17; MSA-26, MSA-28, IDB-14, C-BS-3).
697	- **If `scr_a` is read on A's dead bus (EC-BS-17)**: every lantern is dark, `scr_a`'s and `pump_a`'s alike, and the room's O2 and temperature cannot tell an unpowered healthy scrubber from a FAILED one; the closed-list witnesses falsify "running" and nothing more. A SCAN gives an honest reading (`FIELD_CHECK_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER], scanner in hand), and waking the bus with the spare breaker lights `pump_a`'s lantern while `scr_a`'s stays dark, at the price of the pump-stall clock (90 s) and wear doubled by `DERELICT_FAULT_COMPRESSION`. The world told the player it was dead; SCAN or the woken bus tells them it was broken (BS-17; DA-24, DA-25, AC-DA-111, K4). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* The woken branch buys about 12.9 minutes of unhurried work in the lethal room (DA D.22); the user accepted that modest window as the payoff for waking it (D45), and Derelict Authoring's X-DA-8 reasons log may later trigger one authored payoff that only a served branch delivers. Attention's locus-body pass condition for derelict A is option (b), a fault that wakes when its bus is served (`j_a_main` once fed), confirmed under D47.
698	- **If a stub is never capped, across a restore (EC-BS-18)**: `stubs[]` persists, the hiss persists and nothing forces anything; the leak is a standing consequence-channel truth, bounded by dormancy on a departed derelict (BS-8; IA-26, LS-17, WM-24).
699	- **If two seats target the same node or the same stub (co-op hook) (EC-BS-19)**: the second `begin_cut` is `BUSY` (one job per `(subject_ref, verb class)`), and a second `begin_cap` on a capped stub is `INVALID_TARGET`; the first lit `pickup` of the yield wins and the other seat's is `BUSY` or finds the item gone (BS-7; IA-34, IA-26).
700	- **If the player opens `door_a_spine_machine` and leaves it open (EC-BS-20)**: the "one lethal room" statement is a build-state invariant, so opening the door lets conduction mix the cold into `a_spine` (authored `T0` -12000 mC) for as long as it stays open; the lint prints the open-door projection, the tell stays the frost fan over the sill, and shutting the door behind (a bare-hand V4) is the player's containment act, with its cost on the way out (BS-10; DA-28, DA D.18).
701	- **If a cut node is cut again (EC-BS-21)**: the slot is a SALVAGED tombstone and the verb answers `NOT_SALVAGEABLE`; salvage-once is the faucet's whole shape, and the remaining salvage in a room is read from the empty pedestal rect, the scorched kerf and the stubs, never from a count (BS-16; IDB-17, LSG:243, LY-20, ART 7.4).
702	- **If an abandoned module is revisited on a derelict that went dormant (EC-BS-22)**: the module is in `loose[]` where it was left and the derelict stands as left; if it was dropped in the dark it needs light to re-take, and a dormant room's temperature and gas stand still until the player returns (BS-13, BS-16; LS-17, WM-24, WM-25, WM-28, IA-28).
703	
704	### D. Tells, breach and retreat
705	
706	- **If a tell opens as the cut begins (EC-BS-23)**: the cut completes (240 ticks is well under the played draw), leaving `T - 240` ticks; at the shortest played draw (`TELL_DRAW_LO` 900 [PLACEHOLDER]) a 13-tile carry fits by 36 ticks and a 14-tile carry does not, and at the 600-tick fixture floor 7 tiles is the most; drop-and-run always fits. The cut is loud and forfeits the stillness abort while it runs (BS-7, BS-13; D.3, AT-8, AT-10). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* Under the ruled carry intake the sortie's own tell opens 318 ticks into the carry *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)* and not as the cut begins (D.2), so this case is the fixture-armed contract case (`attention_arm_tell`).
707	- **If a tell opens during the carry and the route is longer than the window (EC-BS-24)**: the decision is the player's, keep walking to the console or set the module down and run at `V_RUN` 3 against `V_CARRY` 1, and both are legal; the module persists where it fell, and re-taking it needs light. A drop is free (exempt from the lit rule), so a false alarm costs time and not the haul (BS-13; IA-28, PC-8, AT-8). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(the decision is the ruled shape: the tell opens inside the carry, holding cargo never outwaits it and a drop does; its margin is thin, 140 permille of the tell draw at 28 tiles, and the pass line is the boarding spike's, D.2, D.3, OQ-BS-27)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
708	- **If a BREACH is running and the carrier reaches the console (EC-BS-25)**: the hop is always allowed, `carry_ref` travels, and the departure ends the BREACH when the last recorded occupant leaves a non-home locus body; the hop pushes no stimulus and does not interrupt a TELL. The hop is the escape verb with the module still in the arms (BS-12, BS-13; WM-26, AT-22).
709	- **If a horror is met during a carry (EC-BS-26)**: nothing kills it, and the MVP kit has no repel tool (user ruling X6; HE-39 is dormant), so the answer is retreat, stillness, darkness or 'drop the cargo', which the user confirmed as the intended price of hauling (D63: in Horror's figures a carrier who keeps the cargo is struck on 7 of 18 draws, with `R_SNAP_PX` 48 the lever) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Horror places nothing in salvage and has no edge to author (HE:376), so no rule here changes with a horror's presence (BS-13, BS-24). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Precondition:** the lengthened decision carry runs through `a_spine`, a single 3-wide corridor with no side step, so the legal exits hold only if a horror does not path or block it at the MVP; until Derelict Authoring and Horror state it (ASK-BS-H1, OQ-BS-33) this row assumes it does not, and if it may, a bypass or a wider spine is required.
710	- **If the player cancels a cut and goes still to abort a tell (EC-BS-27)**: the tell aborts after 594 ticks from an entry at `theta` and 630 from the level ceiling, against a ledger that keeps the partial for `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER] 600 inclusive; the partial survives only an immediate resume at the lowest entry levels, so the cut restarts from zero. Restraint costs the partial and keeps the module in place (BS-7; D.3, IA-16, AT-10). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(once the cut has completed there is no partial to lose; under the ruling freezing is priced: with the instance held the carry-state intake keeps `L` above `theta_HOLD`, so the tell can be outwaited only after a drop, D.3, OQ-BS-27)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
711	- **If `pod_hop` applies with a channel open or a cut ledger standing (EC-BS-28)**: the open channel aborts `ABORT(BODY)` and the ledger entry is Interaction's; the leg and settle alone are 945 ticks, longer than `PARTIAL_TTL_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER] 600, so on return the cut restarts from zero `[UNV: Interaction to confirm the ledger expires on global ticks while the derelict is dormant]`. The module is still in place on the derelict (BS-12; IA-40, IA-16).
712	- **If the player hops out and back to shed Attention (EC-BS-29)**: the level is not reset (a hop does not interrupt a TELL and the departure ring is held), each outbound hop costs `HOP_FUEL_ML` [PLACEHOLDER] 400 mL, and a departure ends only a BREACH, not a tell or the level; a hop is a retreat and not a reset (BS-13; WM-26, AT-22, D.6). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* A hop that leaves a derelict locus before the due run does void that run's breach (TELL to CALM, `ABORTED`, rearm set) when every seat recorded at tell entry has gone, so leaving during the warning is the cheapest escape and costs whatever was not yet carried out; a home-ship locus is not voidable by hopping, and 'the lights you left on' is the price (user ruling D46, confirmed).
713	- **If the carrier hops home with the instance held after a tell on the derelict (EC-BS-63)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*: the burden stops when the seat enters the pod. It is pushed only while the salvage is held aboard the non-home locus body where it was taken, never `IN_POD` and never aboard the home body (delegated ruling R5, 'never to carrying at home', read with the creative-director's lean on the re-review; in the fiction, *the web hears the taking at the wreck*, BS-15), and the level then decays in the pod as usual. On the reference carry the tell is resolved before the pod arrives (from the tell's opening, the carry ahead, the console and the pod leg run-quantised to 948 ticks take 2,004 ticks, more than `TELL_DRAW_HI` 1800), by the departure void or the abort (AT-22, AT-10); the level arrives home at 75 percent of `ATT_THRESHOLD` (4,511,793 mAU) with the beam and the lit home ship feeding it in the pod, or 62 percent (3,734,036) with no pod intake, and stands at 4,389,820 or 3,796,361 mAU at the install after the 486-tick home carry: below `theta_HOLD`, with no home-ship tell (AC-BS-123 (e)). Were the burden to run in the pod and at home, the decay would stay suspended, the voided tell's item-keyed rearm would end on the first CALM run that drains the same item's push (AT-10), and a home-ship tell that no hop can void (D46) would open at once on every successful sortie that kept its module; that is why the scope is keyed on place. A shorter carry whose tell is still running when the pod arrives home is voided at its due run all the same, because every recorded seat has left the locus body (AT-22). Attention's AT-3 keys the push on the pickup locus and says 'never for carrying at home'; Attention's AT-3 row and F-26 state that gate (`actor_section` in a non-home locus body, not `IN_POD`); the Controller is asked to declare the push (ASK-BS-C2); the voided tell's item-keyed rearm is not cancelled by this carry, because no `BURDEN` push is drained in the pod or at home (AT-10) (D.2; AT-22, AT-10, OQ-BS-30) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*
714	
715	### E. Light and the dark
716	
717	- **If a module was dropped in the dark (EC-BS-30)**: it cannot be re-taken until something lights it; the player throws a stick before the pickup (throwing is `BUSY` while carrying, channelling, staggered or downed (IA-29), so after the drop it is allowed) or returns with the beam on. The stick lights at landing, never before (BS-5; IA-28, IA-29, IA-6); the throw pushes one `U_LOUD` [PLACEHOLDER] at landing, so re-lighting a dark drop is a loud act (IA-29, IA-33).
718	- **If both start sticks and the shelf are spent (`GLOWSTICK_START_COUNT` [PLACEHOLDER] 2, `a_dock` shelf 2) (EC-BS-31)**: a dropped module outside any light waits for the chest beam, cell permitting; the home airlock's four-stick supply is the resupply for the next sortie, and `MAX_DEPLOYABLES_LIVE` 8 bounds how many live lights can stand at once (BS-5, BS-19; DA-26, EM, IA-29).
719	- **If the cell is exhausted mid-carry (EC-BS-32)**: the beam goes dark; carrying and `drop` need no light, but `pickup` needs light; the console press needs light too and the console is lit by the pod's status glow, so the module is carried to the dock and hopped home whatever the cell (BS-19, user ruling; SE, IA-6) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
720	- **If the cell is spent, no stick remains and the dock console would be unlit (EC-BS-33)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: under the ruling the console is lit by the docked pod's status glow, an ordinary lit fixture, so `lit(console)` holds and `pod_hop` is accepted (`NOT_LIT` cannot occur while the glow stands; a missing or misplaced glow is a build error of the placement lint, BS-19). The player still cannot re-take a module dropped far from the dock in the dark, which costs that module for the sortie and nothing more. Before the ruling this state was a true soft-lock reached by a long lit session (about 4 survey sorties spend the cell, D.10); the cell is now refillable at home by `top_up` (X5), and the mitigations that narrowed the old state (the two-stick shelf, the home four-stick supply, drop-throw-retake with one LOUD report per throw, IA-29) are no longer load-bearing for the hop. The state is covered by the strand cell of AC-BS-92, which must pass (BS-19, C-BS-9; IA-6, DA-26).
721	- **If the player turns the beam off by choice while carrying (EC-BS-34)**: `toggle_beam` is available as an actor verb; the carry spends no cell and the lamp's exposure term leaves the job, but the frost sill and the hazard are seen only in the beam, and the console needs light to press. A dark carry is a legal Pillar 3 trade, not a rule (BS-5, BS-9; PC-8, EM). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* Beam switches are spaced by Emitter State's commit-spacing rule (`SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS`; Default applied 2026-10-27, confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20), D32, with no Lighting exception granted), so a flicker of the lamp is not a free probe; the reason word is Emitter's.
722	
723	### F. Hazard rooms and death
724	
725	- **If the actor is DOWNED in `a_machine` while carrying (EC-BS-35)**: the Controller clears `carry_ref`, Interaction converts the module to a loose item at the foot origin within one tick (its hook runs at divisor 1, IA-28), and `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` 1800 starts (kept at 1800 for the VS-B revive); in the solo MVP a player may take the give-up-and-reload action while DOWNED (user ruling D7) and otherwise death restores from the newest autosave (SL-7, SL-8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, so the module is back on its pedestal if the newest autosave predates the cut, or at the kerf (loose or in the arms) if it followed the cut (EC-BS-42, D.9); either way the player's knowledge of the room is the carry-over. In co-op the loose module persists where it fell (BS-13; PC-9, SE-13, SE-24, SL-7).
726	- **If the player tries to strip `a_machine` (EC-BS-36)**: eight cuts of 240 ticks plus the crossing exceed the room's CRITICAL clock (2226 against 2184 ticks at `T0`), so the room tolerates one purposeful cut and a shuttle and not a strip; the lethal cold is the authored cost of the richer room (BS-17, BS-20; D.4, DA D.10, DA-28).
727	- **If the bus is woken and then `htr_a` is cut (EC-BS-37)**: the cut is legal on a running machine; the room stops warming and relaxes back toward `T_AMB_MC`, the pump-stall clock (on `pump_a`) continues unaffected, and the heater that made lingering survivable is the thing in the player's arms. The player caused it and the Graph's channel shows it (BS-17; LSG:773, DA-28, DA:1163).
728	- **If a module is dropped in B's vacuum room and must be re-taken (EC-BS-38)**: the re-take is another traverse against `RESERVE_S` [PLACEHOLDER] 90 s, and the DA bound for a carried round trip (56 tiles, 497 permille of the reserve) covers the traverse once, so a drop-and-return roughly doubles the exposure; that is a decision the player makes, with the hiss and the draught as the witnesses (BS-20; DA-28, SE D.11, D.4).
729	- **If the actor's vitals fail while `IN_POD` (EC-BS-64)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the statuses run in the pod (user ruling D60, reversing the earlier hold of Suit's air, cell, thermal and counters), so a death in the pod is the Controller's DEAD (PC-9), `carry_ref` clears by the Controller's downed rule, and in the solo MVP the outcome is the restore from the newest autosave (SL-7, SL-8). A save in `IN_POD` stays a soft-gate state (EC-BS-40). In co-op the loose position of a module when a crewmate is downed in a pod is Web Map's and the Controller's to define (VS-B). The pod leg is part of the sortie's physical budget (D.10, OQ-BS-32).
730	
731	### G. Save, restore and autosave
732	
733	- **If a restore lands mid-carry (EC-BS-39)**: `carry_ref` and the Suit's carried instance are restored together and cross-checked (`SUIT_RESTORE_CARRY_MISMATCH` on a mismatch), the Interaction `post_restore` never touches `carry_ref`, and a channel in progress is dropped (`RESTORE` abort; the Controller maps `CHANNELLING` to `IDLE`). A cut that completed before the autosave stands; one that did not is as if never begun (PC-17, SE-13, IA-15, IA-28).
734	- **If a restore lands in `IN_POD` (EC-BS-40)**: the mid-transit state follows Web Map's restore rules (the persisted leg parameters), `carry_ref` is restored with the Suit's instance, and the module is still in the arms on arrival; a save in `IN_POD` happens only after `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` as a `RISKY` write because `IN_POD` is a soft-gate state (BS-21, BS-12; SL-5, WM-30, PC-17; K15).
735	- **If an autosave lands mid-carry (EC-BS-41)**: it is legal, because `CARRY_WALK` is not a gate state; the restore point is the carry, with the cut done and the stubs hissing, and the loss window of a later death is the carry only (BS-21; D.9, SL-5).
736	- **If the player dies after an autosave that followed the cut, or before it (EC-BS-42)**: after it, the world restores with the kerf, the hissing stubs and the module in the arms or on the floor, and the loss is the carry; before it, the node is intact, nothing of the take remains, and the player keeps what they learned of the room. Failure costs ship and body, never knowledge (BS-21; SL-7, SL-8, D.9, P5). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* After the restore the threat draws (the tell length, Horror's) are re-keyed per restore epoch (a death restore advances it; a Continue of the newest Save & Quit keeps it, so the draws replay identically; a Continue of any other generation advances it; Save/Load stores it in the per-slot `slot_epoch.bin`, staged before `request_restore`; delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14)*, so a quit or a death cannot steer them, while the Graph's physical failures and the persisted counters replay exactly (user ruling X8, D16); the first RUNNING frame after a death restore carries one plain ship-log line (the HUD's FIRST_FRAME_LINE keyed on `restore_reason = DEATH_STUB`, no death wording; user ruling D15, HUD's and not Boarding's).
737	
738	### H. Hallucination and the field checks
739	
740	- **If a FAILED module's sprite or gauge reads alive (class (b), the MVP lie) (EC-BS-43)**: the module-body channel lies and the consequence channel does not; its lantern stays dark on a live bus, because lamp brightness is a closed-list witness (LSG:44); the decision is made on the closed-list witnesses and, where they cannot discriminate (the dead bus), on SCAN. There is no condition bar to trust (BS-6, BS-15, BS-17; LSG:44, LS-22).
741	- **If a phantom is reached for (class (d), VS-A) (EC-BS-44)**: a phantom has no subject and answers like an unlit object, so reaching for one is not a free oracle, and the junk that is real but dressed as a prize betrays itself by the breath-step, a SCAN, the palette leak or the trip home. Deferred with its blockers (BS-14, BS-15; EM-21, IA-13, SN-21).
742	- **If the stowed `part_hull_plate` is held (EC-BS-45)**: the plate lies in `a_spine` on the reference route, and a player who stows it masks the breath cue for the rest of the sortie, since `cue_load = max(carried_class, stowed_class)` reads HEAVY for any carried module; a pickup is `BUSY` while carrying, so the plate is taken on the way in or on a later hop. At the MVP the breath-step is perception only and records nothing, so no false verdict is stored; "drop the plate first" has no performable verb (ASK-BS-S1) (BS-11, BS-14; SE-28, SE OQ-8, DA-26, C-BS-10). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* With a HEAVY item stowed the actor cannot run (user ruling D18), so a drop-and-run retreat is a drop-and-walk at `V_WALK` 2 for a player who stowed the plate (D.3).
743	- **If a hallucination of an entity (class (a)) or of a crewmate (class (c)) appears during a carry (EC-BS-46)**: it hides the body and never the trail, and the human channel (a crewmate's beam colour and shape, their voice) stays true, so a false alarm costs a drop and a re-take under light, not the haul. Deferred to VS and VS-B (BS-15; SN-20, HE).
744	- **If any hallucination is applied to the cut's noise, the stub's hiss, the load's breath, the carry's pace, the time or the air (EC-BS-47)**: none can be; each price channel is truthful by its owner's rule, and a defect that let one lie is a P4 violation (BS-15; IA-33, LSG:44, SE-28, PC-8).
745	
746	### I. Content, budgets and loaded sets
747	
748	- **If the post-weld sortie to A (S4) is made (EC-BS-48)**: `S_int` is 144 authored subjects against `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` 120, over by 24 (DA OQ-DA-20), which the user's ruling D37 answers by registration by adjacency or proximity, so that only subjects near the actor register and the registered count stays inside the budget (Interaction owns the rule and the radius) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; Boarding seeds no loose item, raises no `P` above `PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE` 24, and a solo sortie holds at most one carried instance, so drops are one per module taken (BS-20; DA-32, IA D.10, C-BS-7).
749	- **If any sortie invariant is checked (EC-BS-49)**: it is checked over all five loaded sets S0 to S4 and both sortie orders, never only the first sortie to A: the route legs are per section and unaffected by what else is loaded, the subject budget is the one that moves (BS-20; DA-32, PF-5).
750	- **If the home pool is under the floor when a haul is installed or a hop is pressed (EC-BS-50)**: an outbound hop is refused `FUEL_LOW` but the module is installable at home; a return hop from a derelict is accepted at any pool, including 0, so no sortie strands a haul (BS-12; WM-20, WM D.4).
751	- **If the arrival cell at the destination is blocked (EC-BS-51)**: `pod_hop` answers `ARRIVAL_BLOCKED`, a defect of the dock's clear cell (`SPAWN_BLOCKED` lint); the module stays CARRIED, the player stays at the console and no cargo state changes (BS-2 step 2; WM-9, WM-15, DA-3).
752	
753	### J. Co-op hooks (Vertical Slice B; solo first)
754	
755	- **If a second and third seat board (EC-BS-52)**: each seat has its own `carry_ref` and its own stowed stacks, pod capacity is the seats (one at MVP, WM-5; the VS-B count is the concept's co-op range, owner Web Map at VS-B), and the haul is a division of labour; nothing in this GDD keys on a single seat (BS-12; PC-8, SE-12, WM-5).
756	- **If a crewmate is DOWNED while carrying (EC-BS-53)**: the Controller clears their `carry_ref` and the module falls at their foot origin; there is no stealing from a crewmate's hands and no reward for harm, and a revive is Interaction's and the Suit's (BS-24 G-8; PC-9, SE-13).
757	- **If a cutter is swung near a crewmate (EC-BS-54)**: a cut channel targets a SALVAGE_MODULE subject and never an ACTOR, so nothing is harmed by accident. Harm to a crewmate is not a choice a sane player can make: it needs a deliberate lit `begin_harm` channel (IA-31) **and is admitted only while the attacker's sanity is system-verified below the harm threshold** (Sanity's `actor_sanity_below_harm_threshold`, which reads the SIM `harm_eligible` bit; a sane actor's attempt is `NOT_ELIGIBLE` and does nothing; SN-11); **the victim sees the attacker's palette leak and sanity tell before eligibility opens** (`tell_on` leads `harm_eligible` by `SAN_TELL_LEAD_S`, SN-10); **and the incident is attributed to the web** (Interaction's call to Sanity's Class B mutator `record_harm_event(actor, victim, tick)` at harm-channel completion, SN-13), not to the player. Friendly fire is lethal by the user's decision ("death is a bitch"), but only the web's work can open it (Pillar 4(c); anti-pillar: no intentional PvP; BS-24 G-1 and G-8; IA-25, IA-31). Vertical Slice B: at MVP (one seat) no target exists.
758	
759	### K. Degenerate strategies
760	
761	- **If the player strips a wreck node by node (EC-BS-55)**: each module is a carried trip, a hop and a walk, the faucet is the authored node list and salvage-once, the left derelict persists as left, and a hazard room is lethal at eight cuts; there is no safe farm and no refill (BS-16; DA-21, IDB-17, IDB-29, D.4).
762	- **If the player cuts several modules in one visit and carries one per hop (EC-BS-56)**: the noise is Attention's whatever the carry (a chain of cuts trips a tell in the fifth cycle with the beam on, D.2), the yields lie where they fell and the derelict persists; the stockpile on the deck is a cost the web hears and not a store the player owns (BS-7; IA-33, D.2).
763	- **If the player stands still aboard to wait out a threat (EC-BS-57)**: listening is a stance and idle pushes nothing, but dwell is Sanity's price: 19 mSU per run net, stage 1 after 315.8 s; there is no refuge in waiting (BS-4; PC-10, SN E1, D.8).
764	- **If the player tries to cut in the dark to dodge exposure (EC-BS-58)**: a dark cut is impossible, the act gate needs the target lit, and a lit job is a visible job in the exposure ledger (BS-5; IA-6, EM).
765	- **If the player seals doors behind them to contain what follows (EC-BS-59)**: it is a legal Pillar 3 act with a cost on the way out (a closed door met while carrying, EC-BS-11); nothing in Boarding forbids it and no content closes a door for them (BS-10; IA-24).
766	- **If the player waits between the cut and the lift (EC-BS-66)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*: nothing is held, so the decay runs and the level the lift starts from falls; at 28 tiles, lit, waits of 0, 300, 900 and 1800 ticks leave live shares of 140, 120, 93 and 66 permille (any lit wait floors at 26), and an 1800-tick wait in the dark leaves none (the tell opens 480 ticks into the carry with 864 ahead, inside every played draw). This is intended: **patience before the lift is legitimate restraint** (P3), and it is priced by the existing rules and not by the burden: Sanity's aboard dwell (19 mSU per run net, 2,850 mSU for a 30 s wait, D.8), the lethal cold if the player waits beside the yield in `a_machine` (D.4), the lamp cell if lit (D.10), and the time anything else has to arrive. The burden does not cover a yield within reach; the decision it prices is the carry's. K3 is asserted over the lit sweep, and the dark wait is reported and not asserted (D.2 K3; AT-5, F-26).
767	- **If the player drops the module at the tell, outwaits it and re-takes the same module (EC-BS-67)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*: the abort completes 810 ticks after the drop standing still lit (600 at the pre-glow dark floor), and the rearm keys on the item (Attention AT-10): re-taking the same module before `rearm_until_T` ends the rearm on that run, so there is no fresh `TELL_REARM_TICKS` immunity; the burden and the suspended decay resume and the tell re-opens about 156 ticks into the resumed carry (`rem` 870 at 28 tiles, so the second tell fits every played draw), and waiting out the whole rearm first only moves the re-opening to about 228 ticks (`rem` 798). This is intended: the player trades about 13.5 s of stillness, Sanity's dwell and the risk of what comes in that time for a carry that fits, which is restraint priced in time and not the cheap freeze the ruling set out to price (X3). A different item leaves the rearm in place (BS-13; AT-10, F-26).
768	- **If the tell opens with the carrier on a door cell or still inside `a_machine` (EC-BS-68)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: a `drop` never lands on a door cell (Interaction's `drop_placement`) and answers `OBSTRUCTED` when every candidate cell is blocked (EC-BS-12), and standing in an open doorway or inside `a_machine` spends the lethal-cold budget (D.4, EC-BS-20), so the drop-and-outwait answer is worse there than in the open spine; at the placeholders the tell opens 318 ticks (about 6.6 tiles) into the carry, and where that falls is Derelict Authoring's placement, which is asked to put a decision reach there (ASK-BS-D4 (d), OQ-BS-31) (BS-13; IA-28, DA-28).
769	
770	### L. Simultaneous rules
771	
772	- **If the cut completes on the run in which the level crosses `ATT_THRESHOLD` and the tell opens (EC-BS-60)**: both happen, because the cut's effect lands at completion only (IA-25) and the tell is drawn at entry from its own stream (AT-8) and neither owner reads the other; the player meets the tell with the yield on the deck and not in the arms, and the choice of D.3 (carry, or drop-free run) is available at once. The LOUD one-shot is part of the intake that opened the tell, which is the "weigh the noise" cost made visible (BS-7; IA-25, IA-33, AT-8).
773	- **If the player cancels a cut on the same tick the actor is staggered or an abort cause fires (EC-BS-61)**: `cancel_channel` wins and the hook finds no record, so the ledger entry is written once by the cancel and the abort cue is not played (IA-15); the stagger itself keeps the module (BS-9; PC-8, PC-9).
774	- **If a tell's abort condition and its breach-due tick fall on the same run (EC-BS-62)**: the abort wins, one transition, and no breach opens; a player who is below `theta_HOLD` for `ABORT_HOLD_TICKS` [PLACEHOLDER] at that run is saved by the margin they earned (BS-13; AT-10).

1144	## Game Feel
1145	
1146	Boarding & Salvage has no input, no frame and no animation of its own (BS-1), so its feel is the feel of **what the composition makes the owners' systems do in sequence**: how long the player is made to stand still before a take, how soon the world answers a cut, how slow and how loud the way home is, and how legal it is to put the prize down. Every number below is either cited from its owner (never restated as ours) or derived from an owner's value by a Formulas entry here. **Units:** 1 tick = 16.7 ms (`TICK_RATE` 60); a tile is `TILE_PX` 48 px; speeds are `V_WALK` 2, `V_RUN` 3 and `V_CARRY` 1 px per tick (24, 16 and 48 ticks per tile). Every sortie duration is a **lower bound** while the tool-swap time is unregistered (`T_EQUIP`, SN OQ-SN-6). Placeholders carry the owner's tag. The target emotion is **a held breath, then a heavy walk**: slow, deliberate, exposed, with one door out that is always open.
1147	
1148	### Feel reference
1149	
1150	**Borrow:** *Project Zomboid*'s carried burden that changes how you move and its timed contextual actions (a linear bar, cancelled by moving, no skill check); the hands-free chest lamp of *Pandorum* (the beam stays on the job while both hands work and while they are full); *Lethal Company*'s run back with hands full and the real story of dropping the scrap to survive; *Alien: Isolation*'s stillness as a strategy. **Anti-reference:** a numeric weight readout or mass-scaled speed (Zomboid's moodle), a repair minigame or quick-time event (a UI surface that could leak module-body truth and a rhythm demand the "I can leave now" test forbids), a motion tracker (an Attention meter in another form, AT-20), and any treasure framing (a pickup glow, a reward chime, a sting).
1151

1174	
1175	### Weight (the carry is the felt cost)
1176	
1177	- **The ratio is the feel.** Carry : walk : run is **1 : 2 : 3** in px per tick and **3 : 2 : 1** in ticks per tile (48, 24, 16). A 13-tile frame is crossed in 5.2 s walking and 10.4 s carrying. Noise per tile is **24 AU walking, 48 AU carrying, 64 AU running** (`NOISE_PER_TICK` walk 1, carry 1, run 4 [PLACEHOLDER], D.1 and D.2; locomotion only, and a salvage carry aboard the wreck adds 336 AU of burden per tile, D.2 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)*): carrying is the slowest *and* louder-per-tile than walking, and running is the loudest. Because speed never changes with mass, the 6 kg core and the 90 kg cell feel identical in pace; the difference is the breath (SE-28) and nothing else.
1178	- **No ramp, no slide.** Carry starts and stops instantly like the walk (PCI Game Feel); there is no acceleration curve to read as weight. The weight is the *constant* low speed.
1179	- **Hands full is a verb loss.** On pickup every prompt in the world vanishes except `G . Drop` and, at a fitting hardpoint or the console, its one press (BS-9). The player feels the carry as a narrowing of what the world offers, not as a number.
1180	- **The pace is the lesson.** A trail, a draught or an alarm sweep that outruns a carrier teaches retreat without text (ART 2.8): at `V_CARRY` the web's propagation is faster than the player; at `V_RUN` after a `drop` it is not.
1181	- **The body tells the truth.** Stagger is an input lock and an animation, never a shove; a carry stagger keeps the module; the walk-only cap at CRITICAL vitals is read off the visor fog and the breath (PCI), never a banner.
1182	
1183	### Snap targets (what is one frame, and what is never eased)

1186	|---|---|---|

1188	| Loose sprite to carried sprite | same frame | no fly-to-inventory; no inventory exists |
1189	| Carried sprite to seated machine | one frame | the install is a seat, not a flourish |
1190	| Cap piece appears and the medium ends | same tick | the consequence ends when the act ends (P1) |
1191	| Open-end medium starts | the tick the cut completes | the price is visible at once |
1192	| Work loop and sparks stop | the tick the cut completes | no recoil or overshoot (IA recovery 0) |
1193	| Yield settle | none at MVP; VS optional at most 6 ticks, a 4 px drop, no bounce | no eased motion near a salvage node (G-5) |
1194	| Prompt hide | the same render frame the target is lost or unlit | a prompt for an unlit object would lie |
1195	| Rejection | a cut and a dull cue; no shake, flash or red | rejections never decorate (IA V-10) |
1196	| Full-frame effects on cut, hop, breach, pickup | none | HR-13 and the no-flash rule |
1197	
1198	### The three rhythms of a sortie
1199	
1200	1. **Boarding rhythm (ART 2.6).** Cold, dead, patient. The player is made to stand still before they are allowed to act: the arrival room offers only the beam, dust, a dried trail and the hull's creaks, and every action after it costs light. Target dwell before the first cut: the player chooses; the design target is that **a player who pauses 2 s or more before the first cut is typical**, not forced (X-BS-2). Nothing moves unless the player moves it.
1201	2. **The tell (ART 2.7).** Beam, ambient, radius, temperature and direction do not change; only the rim of the cone gets busier. The tell is **10 to 30 s** by Pillar 2 and in play **15 to 30 s** (`TELL_DRAW_LO` 900 to `TELL_DRAW_HI` 1800 [PLACEHOLDER]); a carry begun at tell entry covers at most 18 tiles (`tell_window_fit`, D.3), so a carry still ahead of more than 18 tiles when the tell opens cannot beat the shortest tell; under the ruled shape the tell opens 318 ticks into a carry of about 21 to 28 tiles, so the *decision* "keep walking with it, or set it down" is live in kind and thin in margin (140 permille of the draw at 28 tiles; the pass line is the boarding spike's, AC-BS-132) (D.2, D.3, **OQ-BS-27**) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R5)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. A cut begun at tell entry completes (240 ticks) and leaves 660 ticks, 13 tiles.
1202	3. **The breach (ART 2.8).** Controlled panic. Alarm Red sweeps for 2 to 3 s, a failure trail runs along a graph edge faster than a carrier walks, and the answer the world teaches is *drop it and go*. `drop` is free; the run at `V_RUN` 3 is three times the carry; the console is one press; the hop is always allowed. There is no forced drop and no refusal (BS-13).
1203	
1204	### The emotional arc of the reference sortie (design-time, not a meter)
1205	
1206	Mapped to BS-2's steps and the art bible's rhythms. Times are illustrative targets for the reference sortie (`htr_a` to `hp_cargo_heater`), not lints.

1210	| Pod leg out | smallness, anticipation | ART 2.5 | the only exterior; an intentional flow break |
1211	| Arrive, stand still | forensic curiosity under a held breath | ART 2.6 | flow entry: low challenge, high attention |
1212	| Read and decide | curiosity turning to appetite | ART 2.6 / 6.5 | competence: reading witnesses |
1213	| Cut (4 s) | commitment; a small guilt at the noise | ART 2.6 to 2.7 edge | the peak of agency |

1268	## UI Requirements
1269	
1270	Boarding & Salvage has **no screen, widget or menu of its own** (BS-1, BS-24). It has UI *content*: the composition rules of the sortie decide which of the HUD's existing surfaces are allowed to show what, and, more often, what they must leave empty. Every surface below is owned by another system (Interaction's prompt plate and bar, the HUD & Suit Layer's hand rail and suit panel, Web Map's console and Chart Table, Save/Load's single cue); Boarding states the content constraints that the UX pass must honour. The first constraint is the one that defines the whole section: **the sortie's UI is mostly what is absent** (G-5, G-6, R-BS-11).
1271

1286	
1287	- **Redundant channels.** The identity of a loop at an open end is redundant with shape (diameter and fitting remnant), not hue alone (ART 4.0 principle 2; R-BS-5); the carry state is redundant between the hand-rail glyph, the raised-hold sprite and the prompt set.
1288	- **The load cue is audio-first, and the ruled package answers it in part** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The Suit's weight cue is breath with a load signature (SE-28), and its blind-identification test is audio (SE RK-2). The user accepted the Suit accessibility package (X10, D44): the `cap.suit.*` caption ids; the rule that haptics driven only by the player's own true body cues are not Attention indicators (added to Adaptive Audio AA-42); and the exceptions E1 (stowed MEDIUM load) and E2 (heat STRAINED to CRITICAL). A deaf or muted player in the dark also gets an opt-in haptic pulse on the tell's beats that carries the same information as the audio (D51). The visual correlate of the load signature (a deeper, slower pack rise under HEAVY, Visual/Audio F-7) stays **not adopted**. The accessibility tier is *standard*, and `design/accessibility-requirements.md` is to be authored later with `/ux-design` accessibility (noted here, not created). OQ-BS-21 is resolved to this package; whether the load breath has a caption id is Suit's.

1290	- **Hold versus toggle.** The cut, cap and scan are channels, hold by default with the Controller's toggle option; leaving is always free (release or move).
1291	- **Remapping.** `drop`, `toggle_beam`, the equip slots and `interact` are rebindable per the Controller's PC-2 table; the sortie's prompts render the active binding.

1294

The UX pass runs through Interaction's and the HUD & Suit Layer's specs, not through a Boarding screen.
1296	
1297	📌 **UX Flag — Boarding & Salvage**: this system has UI content but no screen of its own. In Pre-Production, the specs that must cover it are `design/ux/hud.md` (the carry-state prompt set of BS-9 and the blank on every other target, the LONG and MEDIUM channel bars for the cut, cap and scan, the hand-rail carry state and glowstick count, and the explicit absence list: no weight, capacity, value, condition, timer or Attention readout) and the in-world pattern library (the open-end piece, cap piece, kerf and shared carried-module sprite as text-free affordances), reached through the Interaction and HUD & Suit Layer UX passes.
